On September 15, 2026, Deportivo Alavés hosted Valencia in a La Liga fixture that promised high intensity and tactical discipline. The match remained finely balanced for long periods as both managers searched for a way to break the deadlock under the pressure of a demanding league campaign. VAR Intervention and Early Friction The contest ignited early when Valencia thought they had taken the lead in the 17th minute. Arnaut Danjuma found the back of the net, but after a tense VAR review, the referee ruled the goal out for offside. The frustration of the decision boiled over shortly after, as Antonio Blanco and Javier Guerra both received yellow cards for violent conduct during a heated exchange on the pitch. Deportivo Alavés attempted to assert themselves through Antonio Martinez , who was frequently caught in the offside trap, and a dangerous header from Ville Koski just before the break. However, Valencia goalkeeper Stole Dimitrievski was equal to the task, comfortably handling the aerial threat to ensure the first half ended without a score. Rioja's Impact and Late Drama The second half saw a series of tactical adjustments, including the introduction of Luis Rioja in the 63rd minute. This substitution proved to be the turning point. In the 78th minute, Javier Guerra turned provider, delivering a clinical assist for Luis Rioja , who fired home with his right foot to give Valencia a crucial lead. It was a clinical finish that rewarded the visitors' persistent build-up play. As the clock ticked toward full-time, Deportivo Alavés threw everything forward. Lucas Boye saw a powerful header saved by Dimitrievski in the 93rd minute, and a late effort from Youssef Enriquez flew wide of the target. Despite the late pressure and a 95th-minute offside call against Danjuma on a counter-attack, Valencia held firm to secure a hard-fought 1-0 victory.
